brief: Oracle's 2056 bonds hit a record 8.16% yield, and its CDS hit an all-time wide, after the company issued a force majeure on its New Mexico 'Project Jupiter' data center, citing unresolved power and permitting problems: rejected pipeline routes, no air permits, and the removal of land/power partner BorderPlex. Because 8.16% trades where B3/B- junk credits trade, and S&P/Moody's already cut Oracle to one notch above junk in July, the move implies another downgrade is likely, which would reprice Oracle's $120bn bond stack and spill into the hyperscaler complex. Barclays calls the lease's financial impact 'de minimis' and Goldman frames the filing as legal protection rather than Oracle walking away from the capacity, but the deferred rent extends the lease term so the total owed doesn't fall, and Barclays still expects hardware capex delayed by ~$30bn, which could force Goldman to trim its just-raised $1.2 trillion AI capex forecast. Goldman's own analyst still closes downbeat, warning that third-party AI infrastructure isn't the bond-like asset it can appear to be. The ~20 banks financing the project's $18bn construction loan are sitting on $2bn+ of unsyndicated paper losses, and developer-owner Blue Owl's stock has tumbled to two-month lows.
